metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (pricing.cpp) with a deployable entry point (main()), a Dockerfile, and Kubernetes deployment manifests present.
metadata.archetype_justification: No database connections, no cache writes, no message queue producers. All operations are read-only GET requests returning computed pricing from a static flat file.

findings.title: No network security configuration
findings.description: No network security configuration found in the repository. No VPC, subnet, security group, or NetworkPolicy definitions. The k8s Service is ClusterIP but no NetworkPolicy restricts ingress/egress.
findings.gap: No network segmentation, no security groups, no NetworkPolicy. The service has no defined blast radius limitation.
findings.recommendation: Add a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy to restrict ingress to only authorized callers. Ensure the EKS cluster runs in a VPC with private subnets and least-privilege security groups.

findings.title: No CI/CD automation
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline configuration found. The Makefile has a manual install target using scp to copy the binary to a production server.
findings.gap: All deployments are manual. No automated build, test, or deploy stages. No quality gates.
findings.recommendation: Create a CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions, CodePipeline, or GitLab CI) with stages: build Docker image, run smoke tests, push to ECR, deploy to EKS.

findings.title: Single tightly-coupled CGI binary
findings.description: Single C++ CGI binary with all logic in one file and one main() function. No module boundaries, no separation of concerns.
findings.gap: Tightly-coupled single binary with no architectural structure. No ability to independently scale or evolve individual concerns.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite as a properly structured modern service with separated concerns (handler, service layer, data access). Given trivial size, a full microservices decomposition is unnecessary.

findings.title: Data stored on local filesystem
findings.description: Pricing rules stored in a local flat file (/etc/pricing/rules.dat) — a pipe-delimited text file read from the container filesystem. No managed object storage.
findings.gap: Data locked to local filesystem. No durability, no accessibility outside the container, no versioning.
findings.recommendation: Migrate pricing rules to S3 (with versioning) or DynamoDB for real-time access. Use S3 event notifications or DynamoDB Streams to propagate changes.

findings.title: No database engine version management
findings.description: No database engine used — data stored in an unversioned flat file. No version management, no migration tooling, no lifecycle management for the data layer.
findings.gap: Data layer has no versioning, no schema management, and no lifecycle tooling. Pipe-delimited format is undocumented with no validation.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a managed database (DynamoDB or RDS) with explicit schema versioning and migration tooling.

findings.title: No integration or automated tests
findings.description: No automated tests of any kind. README states 'No tests; correctness validated by spot-checking output.'
findings.gap: Zero automated test coverage. Any change risks silent regression.
findings.recommendation: Create integration tests exercising the CGI endpoint: verify correct pricing for known SKUs, verify 0.00 for unknown SKUs, verify quantity multiplication. Run in CI.

findings.title: No API entry point configured
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, or CloudFront configured. The k8s Service exposes the CGI endpoint directly as ClusterIP with no managed entry point.
findings.gap: No managed entry point providing throttling, authentication, or request validation.
findings.recommendation: Configure an AWS ALB Ingress Controller or API Gateway in front of the service with throttling and request validation.

findings.title: No auto-scaling configured
findings.description: No auto-scaling. K8s Deployment specifies static replica count of 2 with no HPA.
findings.gap: Static capacity — cannot respond to traffic spikes or scale down during low demand.
findings.recommendation: Add a Kubernetes HPA targeting CPU utilization or request latency metrics.

findings.title: No multi-AZ fault isolation
findings.description: K8s Deployment has 2 replicas but no pod anti-affinity rules or topology spread constraints. Both pods could land on same node/AZ.
findings.gap: No guarantee replicas are distributed across Availability Zones.
findings.recommendation: Add topologySpreadConstraints or pod anti-affinity rules to distribute across AZs.

findings.title: Partial IaC coverage
findings.description: Kubernetes manifests define deployment topology. No IaC for monitoring, alarms, dashboards, HPA, or underlying EKS cluster.
findings.gap: No IaC for operational resources (alarms, dashboards, HPA) or networking. Coverage limited to deployment manifests.
findings.recommendation: Add IaC for operational resources: CloudWatch alarms, dashboards, HPA configuration.

findings.title: Legacy C++ with pre-C++11 patterns
findings.description: C++ (pre-C++11 style) compiled with GCC 12. Uses unsafe C string functions (strcpy, strtok), CGI framework, no AWS SDK or cloud-native libraries.
findings.gap: Compound legacy signals: pre-C++11 coding patterns, ancient CGI framework, no AWS SDK integration.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite in a modern cloud-native language (Python, Node.js, Go). The service logic is trivially small (~70 lines) making a rewrite low-effort.

findings.title: No API versioning strategy
findings.description: No API versioning. Endpoint at /cgi-bin/pricing.cgi with no version path, no version headers, no versioning scheme.
findings.gap: Any breaking change would break all consumers simultaneously.
findings.recommendation: Implement URL-path versioning (e.g., /v1/pricing) when rewriting as a modern API.

findings.title: Hardcoded configuration in source
findings.description: Pricing rules file path hardcoded in source (/etc/pricing/rules.dat). K8s ConfigMap defines PRICING_RULES_PATH but the C++ code ignores it.
findings.gap: Hardcoded configuration. No externalized configuration pattern despite ConfigMap being available.
findings.recommendation: Read configuration from environment variables when rewriting. The k8s ConfigMap already provides the values.

findings.title: No data access abstraction layer
findings.description: Single function (lookup_price) handles data access with raw C file I/O. No abstraction, no data contract, no separation from storage implementation.
findings.gap: Raw file I/O with no abstraction. Changing data source requires rewriting with no interface contract.
findings.recommendation: Implement a data access interface abstracting storage mechanism from business logic when rewriting.

findings.title: No API authentication
findings.description: No API authentication. CGI endpoint is open — no auth middleware, no API key, no token verification.
findings.gap: Unauthenticated API endpoint. No access control on pricing data.
findings.recommendation: Add API authentication via API Gateway authorizer (Cognito or Lambda authorizer) when exposing externally.

findings.title: No centralized identity integration
findings.description: No identity provider integration. No Cognito, OIDC/SAML, or IdP federation.
findings.gap: No centralized identity. Authentication, if added, would be standalone.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with a centralized IdP (Amazon Cognito or organizational Okta/Ping) when adding authentication.

findings.title: No vulnerability scanning or patching automation
findings.description: Container hardening present (non-root, drop capabilities, Alpine). No vulnerability scanning, no patching automation, no Dependabot/Renovate.
findings.gap: No systematic patching strategy or vulnerability scanning. Base image updates are manual.
findings.recommendation: Add container image scanning (ECR scanning, Trivy in CI). Configure Dependabot or Renovate for base image tracking.

findings.title: No application security pipeline
findings.description: No security scanning tools configured. No SAST, no dependency scanning, no container scanning. No CI/CD pipeline exists to integrate them into.
findings.gap: No automated security validation. Known buffer overflow vulnerabilities go undetected by tooling.
findings.recommendation: Integrate SAST (Semgrep, CodeGuru), container scanning (Trivy), and dependency checking when creating CI/CD pipeline.

findings.title: No distributed tracing
findings.description: No distributed tracing instrumented. No OpenTelemetry SDK, no X-Ray, no trace ID propagation.
findings.gap: No visibility into request flows. Cannot trace requests or diagnose latency issues.
findings.recommendation: Add OpenTelemetry instrumentation with X-Ray backend when rewriting in a modern language.

findings.title: No SLO definitions
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No CloudWatch alarms, no latency thresholds, no error rate monitoring.
findings.gap: No measurable definition of acceptable service levels.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for availability (99.9%) and latency (p99 < 100ms). Implement CloudWatch alarms.

findings.title: No business metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No pricing lookup counts, no SKU-not-found rates, no revenue-impacting metrics.
findings.gap: No visibility into business outcomes.
findings.recommendation: Publish custom CloudWatch metrics: pricing_lookups_total, sku_not_found_count, average_order_value.

findings.title: No anomaly detection or alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no on-call integration.
findings.gap: No proactive detection of failures or degradation.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch alarms for error rate and latency. Integrate with an on-call notification system.

findings.title: Basic rolling deployment only
findings.description: Kubernetes Deployment uses default RollingUpdate with readiness/liveness probes. No canary, blue/green, or traffic shifting.
findings.gap: No staged rollout. Cannot catch regressions before full rollout.
findings.recommendation: Implement Argo Rollouts or CodeDeploy with EKS for canary deployments with automated rollback.

findings.title: No incident response automation
findings.description: No runbooks, no incident response automation, no self-healing patterns.
findings.gap: Incident response is entirely manual and ad hoc.
findings.recommendation: Create runbooks for common scenarios. Implement as SSM Automation documents or structured markdown.

findings.title: No observability ownership
findings.description: No CODEOWNERS, no named alarm owners, no team-specific dashboards.
findings.gap: No clear ownership of monitoring and alerting.
findings.recommendation: Add CODEOWNERS file. Define team ownership and create per-service dashboard with named owners.

findings.title: Containerized workload targeting managed compute
findings.description: Workload containerized with multi-stage Dockerfile and k8s deployment manifests targeting EKS. Legacy Makefile scp install target still present.
findings.gap: No IaC for EKS cluster. Legacy deployment mechanism still in repo.
findings.recommendation: Remove legacy Makefile install target. Ensure EKS cluster is provisioned via IaC in a platform repo.
